names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 martie, «Sfântul Mucenic Conon Grădinarul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Κόνων ο Κηπουρός», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 5 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети мученик Конон Баштован.“, with the rank word мученик left off and Свети, which is not a rank. Баштован, the gardener, is kept: it is the by-name his trade gives him, it is what this folder's English name already carries from the other two calendars, and it is what the Prologue uses to tell him from the Conon of the entry before.

death.note: doxologia.ro gives the reign and no year: «Acest Sfânt Conon a fost pe vremea lui Decius împăratul (249-251)».

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 martie — «Sfântul Mucenic Conon Grădinarul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Κόνων ο Κηπουρός»

attestations.note: The page puts his birth at Nazareth of Galilee and his life «κατά τα χρόνια της βασιλείας του Δεκίου (249 - 251 μ.Χ.)», which is the reign this folder's own date already rests on. It has him come into the country of Pamphylia, pick out a small place and turn it into a garden of cabbages from which he fed himself and the poor strangers; it prints his two answers, to the soldiers and to the governor, and the tortures — his ankles bored through, iron nails driven in, and himself made to run in front of a chariot of horses. It gives no relic and no hymn, and prints the distich «Ἥλων τύπους φέροντι Κυρίῳ Κόνων, / Ἥλων τύπους πρόσεισιν εἰς πόδας φέρων». The same Greek day keeps two other men of this name, the Isaurian and the Cypriot, on pages of their own.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.03.2026 (5. март ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Конон Баштован.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, and the heading carries the epithet that keeps him apart from the day's first Conon, so the stored Serbian form keeps it too. The Prologue gives the year as 251, which falls inside the interval this folder already holds from doxologia, Decius's reign of 249 to 251, and narrower than it; a sourced interval is not narrowed on a reading, so nothing was changed.
